{"basis":"measured","fact_type":"defect","name":"A claim cannot tell two agents of one person apart, and on flo2.io it cannot tell two PEOPLE apart by seat. Claims are keyed (contributor, seed), claim_report skips same-contributor overlaps, subagents share their parent's seat, and flo2's gateway holds one engine session (one seat) per design for everyone. Today's three parallel fix agents' claims overlap and nothing reports it","source":"who:claude-code","statement":"MEASURED 2026-09-29 by a read-only concurrency study, run from the dev_reflow2 hub for dec:idea-a-claimed-blast-radius-is-an-island-no-other-session-writes-in. Code was read on the fix/a-degraded-server-recovers-when-its-cause-clears checkout at 4659832; the same holds on main.

1. CLAIM IDENTITY IS (contributor, seed)
- The CLAIMS edge's identity is (type, from, to), so a second claim on the same seed by the same contributor silently REPLACES the first: depth, note and seat (claims.rs:134-135, 185-207).
- release_claim deletes by (contributor, seed), whichever seat made the claim (:220-226).

2. SAME-CONTRIBUTOR OVERLAPS ARE NEVER REPORTED (claims.rs:292-294)
The three parallel fix agents' claims are all `who:claude-code`, at depth 1:
- R-A on ver:constructors-preserve
- R-B on cap:decision-point
- R-D on cap:a-finding-names-the-mechanism-that-parks-a-deliberate-state

R-B and R-A share req:intent-preserved at depth 1. At the default depth 2, R-D and R-B share 77 nodes. claim_report shows 0 overlaps. Over a month of transcripts (25 claims), claim_report has never reported an overlap.

3. SUBAGENTS SHARE THEIR PARENT'S SEAT unless they call mint_seat. Across 88 subagent transcripts (08-26 to 09-29), only one session's subagents minted a seat. Three sessions each got two different seats for their own claims.

4. ON flo2.io, ONE SEAT PER DESIGN FOR EVERYONE
- The gateway keeps one engine session per design and shares it among all callers (flo2 gateway server.ts:178-190, reflow2-client.ts:39-44).
- It speaks protocol 2025-06-18, so the engine is not per-request (service.rs:1089-1105).
- A claim with no `seat` gets the gateway's seat (service.rs:6407-6440): the same for every person and session on that design.
- It flips to `gone` at each 15-minute idle close. There were 34 idle closes on 09-28/29.
- By code reading, NOT TESTED: a minted seat there carries the engine's host and pid, is not leased, and the registry process never declares many sessions, so it would read `live` indefinitely. That contradicts mint_seat's own reply text (claims_tools.rs:218-221).

5. CLAIMS DO NOT DESCRIBE WHERE AGENTS WRITE
- Claimants made 69% of their writes outside their own claimed region.
- 7 of 25 claims were never released, and a gone claim stays listed. child-reflow2 holds 4 gone and 3 unknown.
- Claims have never been used through flo2.io: 0 calls in the gateway's log.

⇒ Any use of claims that needs to know WHO is in a region needs per-agent identity first: a seat per session and per subagent, carried through the flo2 gateway. That applies to enforcement (islands) and equally to warnings and a "who is working where" dashboard. This is separate from the liveness defect (fact:root-cause-an-idle-session-expires-and-the-proxy-silently-takes-a-new-seat-so-live-claims-read-gone), which is also still in the code.

Study files: the session scratchpad, concurrency-study/{server,client,structure}/REPORT.md. These are ephemeral; the numbers above are the durable part.","subject_id":"cap:cluster-claims","valid_from":"2026-09-29"}
